title: The Archive of the Rust Belt
premise: Quentin Delacroix has spent eleven years alone on Meridian Station, tending a terraforming garden for colonists who will never arrive, recording daily logs into an archive no one reads. When she discovers her own name—misspelled, unfamiliar—on the manifest of the Calypso, a colony ship that never launched, she realizes someone erased the crew's deaths and hers was among them, meaning either she is not who she believes, or someone wanted her forgotten. Pursued by a salvage syndicate that profits from the station's 'abandoned' status, Quentin flees toward the relay at the edge of dead space to broadcast the true manifest before the jump window closes, gathering three other 'ghosts' the archive reveals were also written out of history. At the relay she must choose between transmitting the truth, which dooms the found family she's built by exposing their erased pasts, or staying invisible forever; she transmits, and in the aftermath the four ghosts claim their real names together as the first honest signal leaves dead space.
about_author: Petra Lockridge is the pen name of a former industrial archivist from Youngstown, Ohio, whose family worked three generations in steel before the mills closed. She writes science fiction about places the future abandoned, drawing on rust-belt oral histories collected from her grandmother's union hall.

chapters.title: Greenhouse Eleven
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She tends the terraforming garden on Meridian Station, narrating her 4,000th daily log to colonists who never came, establishing her rituals, her loneliness, and her stubborn loyalty to a dead mission. The emotional beat is quiet devotion masking grief.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. While cataloguing corrupted ship records, she finds the Calypso's manifest listing 'Quintana Delacroix'—a name almost hers—on a vessel that never launched. Cross-checking, she finds crew death records scrubbed clean. The beat is dread blooming inside routine.

chapters.title: Visitors with Clean Boots
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A salvage syndicate survey team arrives claiming the station is legally abandoned; their leader, Okafor, is too interested in the archive. Quentin hides the manifest chip and plays the harmless gardener. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Ghost Number Two
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Wren, a syndicate comms tech who recognizes the station's beacon signature from records she was ordered to delete—and realizes her own service history has holes too. She secretly warns Quentin via an unlogged channel. Beat: two strangers recognizing shared erasure.

chapters.title: What the Archive Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Digging deeper, she finds four names scrubbed from the Calypso—including Wren's mother—and learns the syndicate falsified the disaster to claim salvage rights over the whole sector. Beat: grief transforming into purpose; the archive becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren calculates the last jump window through dead space in nineteen days and defects, arriving at Meridian with stolen credentials and a warning: Okafor knows about the missing chip. Beat: trust extended across a gun barrel.

chapters.title: Burning the Garden
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Syndicate enforcers board; Quentin torches her own greenhouse to cover their escape, abandoning the garden she kept for people not yet born. They flee on a decrepit tug with two more rescued 'ghosts': old engineer Sefa and teenage stowaway Idris. Beat: sacrifice—the cost of choosing truth over the life she built.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV chapters braided across the tug's silent transit. Systems fail, oxygen runs thin, and each ghost confesses what they lost to the erasure. Idris admits he stowed away hunting the father on the manifest. Beat: found family forged in darkness.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They reach the relay as Okafor's ship closes in; broadcasting the true manifest will expose all four of their erased histories, including crimes Wren committed under orders. With minutes left in the window, Quentin puts her hand on the transmit key. Beat: climax—loyalty versus truth made literal.

chapters.title: First Honest Signal
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Quentin transmits; the manifest floods every receiver in the sector, and Okafor's salvage claims collapse mid-boarding. In the quiet after, the four exchange their true names aloud for the first time, then plant seeds from the burned garden in the relay's hydroponics bay. Beat: resolution—memory restored, family chosen, future replanted.
